items.title: British Pound futures slide as UK inflation trails forecasts.
items.excerpt: British Pound futures fell for the sixth session in the last seven, dropping 2.13% over that stretch to reach their lowest level in nearly a year. During the session, the contract recorded a high of 1.3210 and a low of 1.3136 before finishing the New York cash session down 0.48%. The downward move followed October UK inflation data that came in below the Bank of England forecast ahead of its Dec. 17 policy decision. Headline CPI rose to 3.6% year over year from 3.5%, trailing the central bank projection of 3.73%, while services inflation held at 3.7% and core inflation remained at 2.8%. UK labor market figures also showed signs of cooling as regular pay growth slowed to 3.5% from 3.7% in the three months through September. items.title: Euro FX futures drop for 4th straight session on soft jobs data.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures declined for a fourth consecutive session on Friday, extending a four-day drop to about 1.8% and tracking toward a fourth straight weekly loss of 1.07%. During the session, prices reached a high of 1.1086 before sliding to a low of 1.1038. On the economic front, third-quarter eurozone GDP rose 0.4% quarter over quarter, matching expectations, while quarterly employment remained flat against estimates for a 0.2% increase and annual employment growth slowed from 0.5% to 0.4%. Meanwhile, the European Central Bank reiterated a meeting-by-meeting policy approach while noting higher energy costs could elevate inflation and weigh on growth. Markets currently anticipate December rate hikes from both the ECB and the Federal Reserve, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
